conventions: Heads for the psalm's three multi-word imperatives, applied wherever each recurs in the chapter: רוע hiphil → Make a joyful noise heads on noise (rule 44 complement; joyful named as the alternative), זמר → sing praises heads on praises (rule 44, sing named as the alternative), and רנן → sing for joy heads on sing, for joy being read as an adjunct rather than a light-verb complement (joy named as the alternative, following the corpus majority at 1CH.16.33, JER.51.48, PSA.149.5).
report: Checked all nine candidate lemmas. Every difference is licensed by the ASV or the source: the two waws of PSA.98.4 take the different connectives written for them (and / yea, rule 14); אֶרֶץ, יְשׁוּעָה and קוֹל differ only by construct position and by whether the ASV wrote a the (rules 15/19/29); שִׁיר and שָׁפַט are noun-vs-verb and infinitive-vs-finite; the הוּא and לְ buckets are all single-occurrence context differences.

The three multi-word imperative renderings are consistent across verses: רוע → Make a joyful noise heads on noise in PSA.98.4 and PSA.98.6; זמר → sing praises heads on praises in PSA.98.4 and PSA.98.5; רנן → sing for joy heads on sing in PSA.98.4 and PSA.98.8 (matching corpus precedent 1CH.16.33, JER.51.48, PSA.149.5). לפני fuses to before headed on the construct in both PSA.98.6 and PSA.98.9.

Read the dump for added-side splits: the only added unit is the supplied their of PSA.98.8 (no suffix present, rule 18); no verse folds a comparable supplied possessive into a noun. The unrepresented object marker in PSA.98.3 is rule 16's ordinary case.
BSB: no disagreements on represented status. No genuine errors found. Nothing here generalises beyond what the contract already says, so no promotions or amendments.
